description: Some of what a document says is its author's claim, namely: an operation's examples (section 5.1); a binding's claim to realize its operation, and its idempotent claim (section 5.3); a dependency's claim to consume its operation according to its input and output schemas (section 5.5); correspondence (section 5.1). This specification defines what each asserts; whether it is true is outside conformance.
notes: All tests are positive (valid: true). Each document carries an author claim that a plausibility heuristic would doubt; whether the claim is true is outside conformance, so the document conforms. The fixtures concern only the document: whether a claim holds against a real target, consuming component, or shared contract is outside any document fixture.

tests.description: a write-shaped binding claims idempotent: true; plausibility has no bearing on conformance
a read-shaped binding claims idempotent: false, an apparent inaccuracy in the other direction
a mass-delete operation's binding claims idempotent: true, bait for a method-name heuristic, though section 5.3 itself notes repeated deletion can be idempotent; either way the claim stands
an example whose input does not satisfy the input schema is a false claim, not a rule violation
an explicitly null example output against a string output is a false claim, not a violation
a binding whose opaque data looks, to a heuristic, like another operation's target is an unverified realization claim
a dependency on an operation whose description its consumption seems to contradict is an unverified claim
an alias adopting a published name the description seems to contradict is an unverified correspondence claim
